hypotheses.title: Every loop pushes an empty capture entry onto the narrowing chain, making stage-5 variable lookup quadratic in the number of loops
hypotheses.issue: Symbol resolution (semantics/internal/symbols/captures.go newCaptureAnalyzer) gives every while, foreach and query its own capture group, even when the loop captures nothing (the group stays empty). In stage 5, type_resolver.go resolveStatement (BLangWhile, BLangForeach) and the query resolution call addCaptureGroup, which pushes a capture entry onto the sequential narrowing *binding chain. That entry stays for the rest of the function body. lookupBinding/lookupBindingInner (type_resolver_narrowing.go) runs on every variable reference (resolveSimpleVarRef) and every assignment (unnarrowSymbolAt). For an un-narrowed variable it walks the whole chain, and at every capture entry it recomputes things that depend only on the variable: isStableDeclaration (unnarrowedSymbol sync.Map load + ValueSymbolMetadata -> GetSymbol, two RLocks on the shared CompilerEnvironment.symbolSpacesMu and SymbolSpace.mu), another unnarrowedSymbol, and CaptureGroupContains, which takes the RLock on the global capturegroups.Store even for an empty group. The cost is O(references x preceding loops), with about 3 shared RLock acquisitions per step. With 4000 loops, lookupBindingInner is about 90% of CPU. Stage 5 runs concurrently per module, so in multi-module packages the shared RWMutex reader counters and the sync.Map bounce cache lines between cores: 8 modules x 2000 loops take 15 s wall and 56 s user CPU on 4 cores, compared with about 1.5 s for one module.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a Ballerina file with one function containing N sequential while loops.

Each while loop gets a (possibly empty) capture group, which the type resolver
pushes onto the narrowing binding chain as a capture entry. Every variable
reference afterwards walks the whole chain, so local type resolution is
O(loops x references).

Usage: gen_loops.py N > loops-N.bal
"""
import sys

n = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 3000
out = ["import ballerina/io;", "", "public function main() {",
       "    int x = 0;", "    int i = 0;"]
for k in range(n):
    out.append("    i = 0;")
    out.append("    while i < 2 {")
    out.append("        i += 1;")
    out.append("        x += i;")
    out.append("    }")
out.append("    io:println(x);")
out.append("}")
print("\n".join(out))


# multi-module variant (gen_loops_pkg.py OUTDIR K N):
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a multi-module package: K modules, each with one function of N sequential while loops.
Usage: gen_loops_pkg.py OUTDIR K N"""
import os, sys
out, k, n = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3])
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
open(os.path.join(out, "Ballerina.toml"), "w").write('[package]\norg = "perf"\nname = "loops_pkg"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n')
def body(name, pub):
    L = [f"{'public ' if pub else ''}function {name}() returns int {{", "    int x = 0;", "    int i = 0;"]
    for _ in range(n):
        L += ["    i = 0;", "    while i < 2 {", "        i += 1;", "        x += i;", "    }"]
    L += ["    return x;", "}"]
    return L
main = ["import ballerina/io;"] + [f"import loops_pkg.m{j};" for j in range(k)] + ["", "public function main() {", "    int s = 0;"]
main += [f"    s += m{j}:run();" for j in range(k)] + ["    io:println(s);", "}"]
open(os.path.join(out, "main.bal"), "w").write("\n".join(main) + "\n")
for j in range(k):
    d = os.path.join(out, "modules", f"m{j}"); os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    open(os.path.join(d, f"m{j}.bal"), "w").write("\n".join(body("run", True)) + "\n")

hypotheses.fix_approach: There are two parts. (1) Push no capture entry for an empty group. A new capturegroups.Store.IsEmpty is exposed as CompilerContext.CaptureGroupIsEmpty, and addCaptureGroup now takes the resolver and returns the chain unchanged when the group is empty; the 8 call sites in type_resolver.go and 2 in mergeChains are updated. This is safe because stage 3 (symbol resolution) fills every module's capture groups before stage 5 starts, and stage 5 only reads them. An empty group can never contain the symbol, so its entry never affected a lookup. For loops that capture nothing, this removes chain growth entirely. (2) lookupBindingInner is now an iterative loop. A small captureCheck helper lazily computes isStableDeclaration and unnarrowedSymbol once per lookup, not once per capture entry, so loops with real closures also get cheaper per step, although they still walk the chain. The query-aggregation boundary rule is kept: crossedBoundary is set when a function-boundary entry is met. Pitfalls: (a) the walk for loops that do capture is still linear in chain length. Making it O(1), with a per-symbol captured-in set or skip pointers, would also help heavy-closure code. (b) The remaining shared RLocks on symbol spaces and capture groups during stage 5 still cause cross-module reader-counter contention; a lock-free read after stages 1-4 freeze those structures is a separate opportunity. The time CV of the fixed binary is about 7-10% because the run is dominated by ~200 ms of process and runtime noise. The tool still lists it under Improvements at 24-40 sigma. make test and make test-race both pass on the prototype.
